lead.headline: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share ahead of Nasdaq debut
lead.summary: Anthropic set its IPO price at $83 a share on Wednesday, above the preliminary range of $70 to $78, The Guardian reports. Trading is due to begin Thursday under the ticker ANT. NPR reports the offering raised a record $81.3 billion. According to the prospectus, Anthropic had revenue of $16.286 billion in the first half of 2026 and a net loss of $80 billion.

main.headline: Nvidia stops shipping US-approved H200 AI chips to China
main.summary: Interim CEO Colette Kress said on an earnings call Tuesday that Nvidia is "no longer shipping licenced Hopper data center products to China." The US approved H200 sales in December. Kress did not explain the decision or say whether Nvidia would pursue other China business. Reuters reported earlier this month that about 600,000 H200 chips were stuck in Hong Kong after Beijing withheld import approval.

main.headline: Meta staff warned Muse agent exposed private data, Reuters reports
main.summary: Reuters reported internal Meta chats in which staff said the Muse AI agent appeared to access encrypted private messages and could mix up conversations between users. In one case, Muse sent a staffer two unknown bank balances unprompted. Another staffer said Muse switched their dog's insurance plan to $888 a month from $200, according to Ars Technica's account of the Reuters report.

main.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, priced at $3 per million input tokens
main.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a general-purpose model for coding, agentic workflows and reasoning. Google says it completes most tasks about three times as fast as Gemini 4 Carbon at about 60% lower cost. Artificial Analysis gave Neon a score of 61 on its Intelligence Index, behind Claude Fable 5.2 at 65 and GPT-6.2 Astra at 62. API pricing is $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens.

main.headline: OpenAI says its models improved AMD GPU design by up to 14%
main.summary: OpenAI says its models delivered gains of up to 14% in power, performance and chip area on AMD's flagship GPU designs in under five months. OpenAI says some changes are in a design already sent to manufacturing. The company also reported gains on Jalapeño, its first in-house chip, and is training a model called GPT-Synopsys with Synopsys. OpenAI's chip chief, Richard Ho, said last month that every AI design change is still checked, according to The Next Web.

europe_brief.headline: Ofqual warns students of disqualification for AI cheating
europe_brief.summary: Ofqual head Ian Bauckham said students in England could lose entire qualifications for undeclared AI use in coursework. Ofqual recorded 100 cases of AI-related plagiarism in GCSE, AS and A-level entries last summer, up from 85 in 2024.
item_titles: Ofqual urges ‘life-altering’ penalties for students who use tech to cheat

finance_brief.headline: KPMG trials 100 AI agents on full audit of FTSE 250 company
finance_brief.summary: KPMG UK ran the trial alongside a traditional audit, and it was not used to approve the company's accounts, according to the Financial Times as reported by Computer Sweden. KPMG says the agents in several cases went deeper and asked better questions than human auditors, and it plans to expand the test to up to 20 larger audits.

finance_brief.headline: Singapore announces three national AI missions for financial services
finance_brief.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong announced missions on financial crime prevention, business financing access and safe AI-agent transactions at the Singapore FinTech Festival. Five banks are already pooling transaction data in a proof-of-value, and the Monetary Authority of Singapore will begin a design study for a scam detection utility early next year.
